module.purpose: Defines the static configuration types, defaults, permission rules, and React hooks for the commenting layer.
module.summary: This module establishes the commenting configuration contract, component override points, anchoring behavior, reaction policy, history settings, and permission callbacks. It provides default options plus editor lookups and reactive or non-reactive helpers for determining whether viewers may comment or modify specific records. Permission callback failures are contained, logged, and treated as denials.
module.businessContext: Supports collaborative canvas commenting, including comment ownership, moderation, reactions, pins, and thread actions. Failures can expose unauthorized actions or prevent users from creating and managing comments.

units.name: permits
units.source:
/**
 * Ask a host's permission callback, denying the write if it throws.
 *
 * These are called during render, so an exception in one would take the comments layer down with
 * the answer. Denying costs an affordance, which is what a `false` would have cost anyway, and it
 * can't offer a write a server enforcing the same rule would then reject.

detail.name: permits
preconditions: The supplied permission input is callable according to the function's accepted API.
postconditions: Returns the permission decision when evaluation completes normally.
Returns a denial decision if the permission callback throws.
invariants: A permission callback exception must not escape to the caller.
A callback failure is treated as permission denial rather than permission being granted.
edgeCases: If the permission callback throws during evaluation, the operation is denied and the exception is suppressed.
For a normally completing callback, its permission decision is returned to the caller.

errorPolicy.returnsOnError: A denial decision when the permission callback throws.

detail.summary: Evaluates a host permission callback for a commenting operation and denies the operation when that callback throws.

specTests.then: It suppresses the exception and returns a denial decision.

units.name: getCanComment

detail.name: getCanComment
postconditions: Returns a boolean indicating whether commenting is permitted for the current viewer.
invariants: A throwing permission callback never grants commenting permission.
edgeCases: When canComment is unset, permission defaults to whether currentUserId is non-null.
When canComment is a callback that throws, the result is false.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: A throwing canComment callback is treated as denial rather than propagated.

detail.summary: Determines whether the current viewer may participate in commenting according to the configured commenting options. If no explicit permission is configured, participation is allowed only when a current user is present, and permission callbacks that throw deny access.

units.name: useCanComment

detail.name: useCanComment
postconditions: Returns the permission result produced for the canComment capability.
invariants: The canComment evaluation uses null when currentUserId is nullish.
The permission result is reactive through the permits mechanism.
edgeCases: When currentUserId is null or undefined, the canComment evaluation receives null.
When the relevant signals change, the reactive permission result is re-evaluated.
detail.summary: Provides a reactive permission result for whether the current user can comment in the supplied editor context.

specLiterals.role: Capability key passed to permits and used to identify the comment permission.

units.name: defaultCanModifyComment
units.source:
* The default {@link CommentingOptions.canModifyComment}: a write is its record's owner's to make —
 * a comment's author edits and deletes it, a thread's creator deletes the thread — and a viewer
 * with no identity may make none of them.
 *
 * Exported so a callback can widen the default rather than restate it:
 * `(ctx) => isModerator(ctx.currentUserId) || defaultCanModifyComment(ctx)`.

detail.name: defaultCanModifyComment
preconditions: The callback context identifies the current user and the record or operation whose modification permission is being evaluated.
postconditions: Returns permission consistent with record ownership: comment authors can edit and delete their comments, and thread creators can delete their threads.
A context with no current-user identity does not permit comment or thread modification.
invariants: Permission is restricted to the owning user under the default policy.
No identity never receives modification permission from this policy.
edgeCases: When the current user has no identity, no comment or thread modification is permitted.
When the current user is the comment author, comment editing and deletion are permitted.
When the current user is the thread creator, thread deletion is permitted.
detail.summary: Determines whether the current user may modify a comment-related record under the default ownership policy. Comment authors may edit or delete their comments, thread creators may delete their threads, and users without an identity may perform none of these actions.

specTests.when: The default modification policy is evaluated for editing or deleting that comment.
The default modification policy is evaluated for deleting that thread.
The default modification policy is evaluated for any comment or thread modification.

units.name: getCanModifyComment
units.source:
* This is the per-record rule alone: the built-in UI additionally requires
 * {@link CommentingOptions.canComment}, since a viewer who may not participate gets no action
 * affordances at all.
 *
 * A plain, untracked read — a `canModifyComment` callback that reads signals is not observed. In
 * React, use {@link useCanModifyComment} instead.
 *
 * @public
 */
export function getCanModifyComment(
	editor: Editor,
	currentUserId: string | null | undefined,
	modification: CommentModification
): boolean {
	const { canModifyComment } = getCommentingOptions(editor)

detail.name: getCanModifyComment
preconditions: editor is a valid Editor instance.
modification is a valid CommentModification value.
postconditions: Returns a boolean indicating whether the requested comment modification is permitted for the supplied user identity.
invariants: The result represents the per-record modification rule alone and does not itself require the broader canComment permission.
edgeCases: currentUserId may be a string, null, or undefined; the configured modification rule receives the supplied identity representation.
A user may be permitted or denied for the specific modification independently of whether the user may participate in commenting generally.
detail.summary: Determines whether the specified current user is permitted to perform a given modification on a comment according to the editor's commenting options. This evaluates the per-record modification rule independently of the broader canComment participation rule.

units.name: useCanModifyComment

detail.name: useCanModifyComment
detail.signature: function useCanModifyComment(currentUserId: string | null | undefined, modification: CommentModification): boolean
preconditions: currentUserId may be a string, null, or undefined.
modification must provide an action and the corresponding comment or thread record required by the modification type.
postconditions: Returns the boolean permission result produced by getCanModifyComment for the current editor, user identity, and modification.
Subscribes to value changes using the selected affected record rather than the modification object identity.
invariants: The dependency representing the affected record is the thread for delete-thread actions and the comment for all other actions.
The fresh modification object identity is not itself used as a reactive dependency.
edgeCases: When currentUserId is null or undefined, the underlying permission function determines the returned boolean.
When modification.action is delete-thread, the thread record is selected as the reactive record dependency.
When modification.action is not delete-thread, the comment record is selected as the reactive record dependency.
When modification is recreated with the same action and affected record, the modification object identity alone does not force a dependency change.
detail.summary: Returns whether the current user can modify the specified comment or thread modification. The permission result is reactively recomputed when the editor, user identity, modification action, or affected comment record changes.

specLiterals.role: Selects the thread record as the affected reactive dependency for thread deletion modifications.
